The early production of “Ki Khasi Poems'* or 
"Ki Sur Khasi" is in compliance with the withes of 
the school'Siudenis and friends who have had an 
opportunity of reading some of the Poems published 
in the Khasi papers, or have heard them somewhere. 
Some facts of life are written in verses with a belief 
that “Poetry appeals to, exercises and strengthens the 
feeling of the human heart.*' Poetry may indeed 
be defined as “the fit expression of the fit emotion.** 
The nobel emotion follows on, and is the outcome of 
the deepest ihourht and the truthful view of thinga* 
A poet must see clearly and feel deeply, so that he 
may be able to express his feelings in such a way that 
the same emotions rise in the heart of others. It is 
believed that these Poems will not only widen the 
range of imagination, but will also build up the moral 
character of the youths of our Country. In this Poems 
are embodied many virtues which the young people 
should attain— knowledge of and gratitude to God* 
love for fellowmen, respect for parents and high aspi> 
ration after real progress and advancement in all the 
walks of life. The Poems are written in a pure Khasi 
language commonly spoken by Cherra-Mawsmai people 
with regularity of spelling.

The public and students will, I hope, take pleatare 
in buying this little book in large number. I thank; 
them in anticipation.
